Echidneus.definition: Echidnēus adj., of Echidna (a monster, mother of Cerberus): canis, Cerberus, O.

Eleleides.definition: Elelēides —, f Eleleus, the Bacchae , O.

Euhias.definition: Euhiās or Euiās adis, f , eu)ia/s, a Bacchante, H.

ea2.definition: eā adv. abl f. of is; sc. viā, on that side, that way, there : eā proxime accedi poterat: eā introrumpere, Cs.: transitum eā non esse, L.

eadem.definition: eādem adv. abl f. of īdem; sc. viā , by the same way : ventum est, eādem quā, etc.: revertens, L.: escendens descendensque, S. — At the same time, likewise , T.

ebulum.definition: ebulum ī, n AMBR-, Dane-wort, dwarf-elder , V.

eburneus.definition: eburneus adj. ebur, of ivory : dentes, elephants' tusks : signum: colla, white as ivory , O.

ec-.definition: ec- an indef part., only in compounds.

eccam.definition: eccam i. e. ecce eam; see ecce.

ecfatus.definition: ecfātus, ecferō, ecfor, ecfutuō etc., see eff-.

eclogarii.definition: eclogāriī ōrum, m ecloga, select passages .

ecquando.definition: ec-quandō adv. interrog, ever, at any time: ecquando te rationem redditurum putasti?: quotiens hoc agitur, ecquandone nisi? etc.: quaero ecquando creati sint, etc., whether ever.

ecquid.definition: ecquid adv. interrog. neut. of ecquis.—Direct, at all? ecquid te pudet? T.: ecquid vides, quos, etc.: ecquid sentitis? etc., L.: Ecquid animos excitat Hector? V.—Indirect, whether, if at all : petisse, ecquid hanc rem…

ecquinam.definition: ecquīnam quaenam, quodnam (no gen. or dat.), pron interrog. adj. ecqui + nam.—Direct, Is there any? any? ecquodnam principium putatis? etc. —Indirect, whether any, if any : dubium, ecquaenam fieri possit accessio.

ecquisnam.definition: ecquisnam quidnam (no gen. or dat.), pron interrog. subst. ecquis + nam.—Direct, any one? anybody? Ecquisnam tibi dixerit, etc. — Indirect, whether any one : interrogare, ecquosnam posset nominare.

ecquo.definition: ecquō adv. interrog. ecqui, to any point? to any result? ecquo te provehere?

eculeus.definition: eculeus (equu-) ī, m dim. equus, a young horse, foal, colt : in equo quam in eculeo.— A small equestrian statue : eculeos argenteos aufert. — A rack, torture-horse : facti in eculeo quaestio est.

edendum.definition: edendum ī, n P. of 1 edo, victuals, food : penuria edendi, V.

edictum.definition: ēdictum ï, n edico, a proclamation, ordinance, edict, manifesto (of a magistrate or generalin-chief): consul praetor nova edicta proponunt: civem edicto eicere: proconsulis, L.: rex Edicto vetuit ne quis, etc., H. — E…

editum.definition: (ēditum ī), n editus.—Only plur. — Heights, elevations : montium, Ta., Cu.— Commands, orders : Thaumantidos, O.

edo1.definition: edō ēdī, ēsus, ere, or ēsse (ē st for edit; ēsses, ēsset, for ederes, etc., V., H., O., Iu.; ēstur, O.—Subj: edit for edat, H.; edint, C.) ED-, to eat, consume : de symbolis, T.: ut biberent, quoniam esse nollent: ut …

edo2.definition: ē-dō didī, ditus, ere, to give out, put forth, bring forth, raise, set up: animam, i. e. die: vitam, to end: spiritum: clamorem, utter: voces: questūs, O.: Maeander in sinum maris editur, discharges, L.: ordo editus i…

educo1.definition: ē - dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to lead forth, draw out, bring off, take away: eos nobiscum: (medicum) tecum, i. e. to your province: impedimenta ex castris educi iussit, carried, Cs.: gladium, draw, Cs.: gladiis eductis:…

educo2.definition: ēducō āvī, ātus, āre DVC-, to bring up, rear, train, educate : unā a pueris educti, T.: apud alquem: illum primis cunis, O.: ars dicendi ea educat, develops : educata huius nutrimentis eloquentia.— To produce, support…

effatum.definition: effātum (ecf-) ī, n effatus, an utterance, axiom .

effectum.definition: effectum ī, n P. n. of efficio, an effect .

effectus2.definition: effectus ūs, m ex + 2 FAC-, an effecting, execution, accomplishment, performance : peccare sine effectu, i. e. an outward act : operis, L.: opera in effectu erant, nearly done , L.: spei, L.— An operation, effect, res…

effeminatus.definition: effēminātus adj. with sup. P. of effemino, womanish, effeminate : ne quid effeminatum sit: languor effeminatissimus: vox stupris effeminata.

efferatus.definition: efferātus (ecf-) adj. with comp. P. of 2 effero, wild, savage, fierce : multa: mores efferatiores, L.

efferitas.definition: efferitās (ecf-) ātis, f efferus, wildness, barbarism : omnem ecferitatem expuli.

effero1.definition: efferō or ecferō extulī, ēlātus, ferre ex + fero, to carry out, take out, bring forth, take away, remove : tela ex aedibus: extra aedīs puerum, T.: frumentum ab Ilerdā, Cs.: signa portis efferri vidit, L.: pedem, esca…

effero2.definition: efferō āvī, ātus, āre efferus, to make wild, make savage, barbarize, brutalize : terram immanitate beluarum efferari: speciem oris, L.: gentes inmanitate efferatae: efferari militiā animos, L.: Thebanos ad odium Roman…

effertus.definition: effertus adj. P. of effarcio, crammed, rich : arva Asiae, poet. ap. C.

efficaciter.definition: (efficāciter) adv. efficax, efficaciously, effectually .—Only comp: efficacius agere, L.: obligari, Ta.

efficiens.definition: efficiēns entis, adj. P. of efficio, effective, efficient, producing, active : res: virtus efficiens utilitatis, the producer : ea, quae sunt efficientia voluptatum.

efflagitatus.definition: (efflāgitātus, ūs) m efflagito, an urgent solicitation .—Only abl sing. : meo.

effrenate.definition: effrēnātē adv. with comp. effrenatus, unrestrainedly, violently : incitari: effrenatius in aciem inrupere.

effrenatus.definition: effrēnātus adj. with comp. ex + frenatus, unbridled, without a rein : equi, L.—Fig., ungoverned, unrestrained, unbridled : homines secundis rebus: libido effrenatior, L.: cupiditas: effrenatior vox: ecfrenati libidine.

effugium.definition: effugium ī, n ex + 2 FVG-, a fleeing, flight, escape, avoidance, way of escape, means of flight : mortis: pennarum, by means of : naves peritis nandi dedissent effugium, L.: ad effugium navem habere, L.: in publicum, …

effuse.definition: effūsē adv. with comp. effusus, far spread, in disorder, at random : ire, S.: fugientes, L.: sequi, L.: effusius praedari, L. — Fig., profusely, lavishly, extravagantly : donare: vivere: animus exsultat: hospitiis eff…

effusus.definition: effūsus adj. with comp. and sup, poured out, extensive, vast, broad, wide: late mare, H.: loca, Ta.: incendium, L.—Relaxed, slackened, loosened, dishevelled: quam potuit effusissimis habenis, L.: comae, O.: (nymphae) …

effutuo.definition: effutuō (ecf-) —, ūtus, ere ex + futuo, to exhaust by indulgence : ecfututa latera, Ct.

egens.definition: egēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of egeo, needy, necessitous, in want, poor : egens relictast misera, T.: egentes abundant: delectus egentium, Cs.: nil magnae laudis, not craving , V.: non rationis, not destit…

egregie.definition: ēgregiē adv. with comp. egregius, excellently, eminently, surpassingly, splendidly, exceedingly, singularly : studere, T.: fecerat hoc: vincere, brilliantly , L.: Dixeris, H.: cordatus, Enn. ap. C.: factus: munitum op…

egressus2.definition: ēgressus ūs, m egredior, a going out, going away, egress, departure : vestrum egressum ornando: arcet egressu (ventos), O.: egressūs eius explorat, tracks his movements , S.— A disembarking, landing : optimum esse egr…

ei2.definition: ei interj, oh! alas!: Ei, vereor nequid, etc., T.: Ei mihi, quod, etc., O., V., Ct., Tb.

eiaculor.definition: ē-iaculor ātus, ārī, dep., to shoot out, throw out: aquas, O.: se in altum, O.

eiectamentum.definition: ēiectāmentum ī, n eiecto, refuse, jetsam.— Plur. : cetera maris, Ta.

eiectio.definition: ēiectiō ōnis, f eicio, a casting out, banishment, exile .

eiecto.definition: ēiectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. eicio, to cast out, throw up : harenas, O.: cruorem Ore, V.

eiero.definition: ēierō or ēiūrō āvī , ātus, āre ex + IV-, to refuse upon oath, reject by oath, abjure : id forum sibi iniquum eierare, make oath that the tribunal is prejudiced : me iniquum: bonam copiam, i. e. make oath of insolvency…

eiulatio.definition: ēiulātiō ōnis, f eiulo, a wailing, lamenting : lugubris: non virilis, H.

eiulatus.definition: ēiulātus plur nom., ūs, m eiulo, a wailing, loud lamentation : Philoctetae.

eiulo.definition: ēiulō —, —, āre 2 ei, to wail, lament .

eiusdem.definition: ēiusdem modī, ēius modī see modus.

elaboratus.definition: ēlabōrātus adj. P. of elaboro, highly wrought, finished, labored : versūs: concinnitas: non elaboratus pes, i. e. a simple strain , H.: alqs in verbis, Ta.

elatus.definition: ēlātus adj. P. of effero, exalted, lofty, high : animus: verba, high-sounding : animis superbis, V.: insula opibus, N.

electrum.definition: ēlectrum ī, n , h)/lektron, electrum, an alloy of gold and silver: liquidum, V.: attonitus pro Electro, his plate, Iu.—Amber, a fossil gum from the Baltic sea, O.—Plur: Pinguia, V.

electus1.definition: ēlēctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of eligo, picked, select, choice, excellent : sexaginta (milia armata), picked troops , Cs.: milites, Cs.: exercitūs, Ta.: electissima verba: scripta, Ct.— As subst m. : cum electo …

electus2.definition: (ēlēctus, ūs) m eligo, a choice .—Only abl sing. : necis, O.

elegans.definition: ēlegāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup. for ēligēns, P. of eligo, accustomed to select, fastidious, nice, delicate : heia, ut elegans est! T.: qui se elegantīs dici volunt: elegantissimus poëta, N. — Select, choice, n…

elegeia.definition: elegēia ae, f , e)legei/a, an elegy, elegiac song: elegeia cantet Amores, O.

ellam.definition: ellam for en illam; see en.

ellum.definition: ellum for en illum; see en.

elucubror.definition: ēlūcubror ātus, ārī, dep. elucubro, to work out at night, toil over : epistulam.

elutus.definition: (ēlūtus) adj. P. of eluo, washed out, watery . — Only comp: inriguo nihil est elutius horto, H.

eluvies.definition: ēluviēs —, em, ē, f ex + 3 LV-, an overflow, inundation : eluvie mons est deductus in aequor, O.: maris, Ta.: eluvies iter morabantur, Cu.— A washing away, discharge : conducere Siccandam eluviem, removal of sewage , …

emendate.definition: ēmendātē adv. emendatus, faultlessly, perfectly : loqui.

emendatus.definition: ēmendātus adj. P. of emendo, correct, faultless, perfect : mores: vir, H.: locutio: carmina, H.: emendata maxime.

emeritus.definition: ē-meritus adj., that has finished work, past service: equi, O.: aratrum, O.: acus, Iu.—Plur m. as subst, discharged veterans, Ta.

eminens.definition: ēminēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of emineo, standing out, projecting, prominent, high, lofty : oculi: promunturia, Cs.: saxa, S.: genae leniter: trabes eminentiores, Cs.: per inaequaliter eminentia rupis, irregular s…

emptum.definition: ēmptum ī, n emptus, a purchase, contract of purchase : quae ex empto aut vendito contra fidem fiunt, in buying and selling .

endo.definition: endo praep. old form of in, in : endo caelo, C. (XII Tabb.).

endoploratus.definition: endoplōrātus P. endoploro, old for imploro, to cry for help : endoplorato, ut, etc., a cry for help having been raised , C. (old form.).

enervatus.definition: ēnervātus adj. P. of enervo, unnerved, weakly, effeminate, unmanly : homines: ratio et oratio: sententia.

enimvero.definition: enim-vērō or enim vērō adv., yes indeed, yes truly, assuredly, of a truth, to be sure, indeed: Enimvero Chremes cruciat adulescentulum, T.: enim vero ferendum hoc quidem non est: hic enim vero tu exclamas, etc.: tum e…

enixe.definition: ēnīxē adv. with comp. enixus, strenuously, earnestly, zealously : causam suscipere: Caesarem iuvabat, Cs.: enixius ad bellum adiuvare, L.

enixus.definition: ēnīxus adj. P. of enitor, strenuous, earnest, zealous : studium, L.: virtus, L.

enodate.definition: ēnōdātē adv. with comp. enodatus, lucidly, explicitly : narrare: enodatius explicare.

ensiger.definition: ēnsiger gera, gerum, adj. ensis + GES-, sword-bearing : Orion, O.

enubo.definition: ē-nūbō nūpsī, —, ere, to marry away, marry (to a stranger), L.—To marry out of one's rank: filias e patribus, L.

enucleatus.definition: ēnucleātus adj. P. of enucleo, pure, clean : suffragia, free from undue influence : genus dicendi, unadorned .

enucleo.definition: ēnucleō —, —, āre ex + nucleus. — Fig., to lay open, explain in detail : haec nunc: argumenta.

enuntiatum.definition: ēnūntiātum ī, n P. of enuntio, a proposition .

eo1.definition: eō īvī or iī (3d pers. rarely ī t, V.; inf. īvisse or. īsse), itūrus (P. praes. iēns, euntis; ger. eundum), īre 1 I-, to go, walk, ride, sail, fly, move, pass : In in malam rem, T.: subsidio suis ierunt, Cs.: quocumqu…

eo2.definition: eō adv. old dat. and abl. of pron. stem I-. I. Locat. and abl. uses, there, in that place : cum tu eo quinque legiones haberes.—Fig.: res erat eo iam loci, ut, etc., in such a condition.—Therefore, on that account, fo…

eodem.definition: eōdem adv. of place old dat. and locat. of idem. I. Locat. use; with loci, in the same place : res eodem est loci quo reliquisti.— II. Dat. uses, to the same place, to the same point, thither : clientes suos eodem con…

epiredia.definition: epirēdia ōrum, n e)pi/ + raeda, traces , Iu (acc. to others, carts, wagons ).

epitaphios.definition: epitaphios ī, m , e)pita/fios, a funeral oration.

epodes.definition: epodes um, m a kind of sea-fish, O.

epos.definition: epos (only acc.), n , e)/pos, a heroic poem, H.

equiria.definition: equīria ōrum, n equus, annual races in the Campus Martius, in honor of Mars , O.

erectus.definition: ērēctus adj. with comp. P. of erigo, set up, upright, elevated, lofty : (homines) erectos constituit: voltus, O.: prorae, Cs.—Fig., elevated, lofty, noble : celsus et erectus: ingenium, Ta.: si quis est paulo erectior…

erratum.definition: errātum ī, n 1 erro, an error, mistake, fault : commune: nullum ob erratum: minimum: errata officiis superes, S.: errata aetatis meae.

erratus.definition: (errātus, ūs) m 1 erro, a wandering, winding .— Only abl plur. : longis erratibus actus, O.

erro1.definition: errō āvī, ātus, āre, to wander, stray, rove, roam: cum vagus et exsul erraret: non certis passibus, O.: circum villulas nostras: per urbem, L.—Pass impers.: solis erratur in agris, V.—Of things: quae (stellae) errante…

erro2.definition: errō ōnis, m 1 erro, a wanderer, vagabond : fugitivus erro, H.— A wanderer in love , Tb.

erudite.definition: (ērudītē) adv. eruditus, learnedly, with erudition .—Only comp. and sup: eruditius disputare: litterae eruditissime scriptae.

eruditus.definition: ērudītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of erudio, instructed, educated, learned, accomplished , informed, skilled, experienced : quas (artī s) qui tenent eruditi appellantur: Graeculus: rebus gestis: litteris eruditior …

escaria.definition: ēscāria ōrum, n esca, dishes, plate , Iu.

escensus.definition: (ēscēnsus, ūs) m ex + SCAND-, a scaling . — Only abl sing. : capta escensu munimenta, by storm , Ta.

escunt.definition: escunt old for erunt; see sum.

etesiae.definition: etēsiae ārum, m , e)thsi/ai, Etesian winds, trade-winds, N. W. winds which prevail in summer in the eastern parts of the Mediterranean Sea: venti: etesiis tenebatur, Cs.

eugae.definition: eugae (euge) interj., eu)=ge, bravo! well done! good! hurrah!: eugae habeo optumam, T. — Ironic.: eugae, iam lepidus vocor, excellent! T.

euhans.definition: euhāns or euāns antis P. (the cry of the Bacchantes), crying euhan! Ct., Pr.—Poet. with acc: euhantīs orgia Ducebat Phrygias, celebrating the rites of Bacchus with the cry euhan! V.

evagor.definition: ē-vagor ātus, ārī, dep., to wander forth, march to and fro, manœuvre: effuse, L.: ad evagandum spatium, for evolutions, L. — Fig., to spread, extend: qui appetitū s longius evagantur: late vis morbi, L. — With acc: or…

evalidus.definition: ē-validus adj., very strong, mighty: spina.

eventum.definition: ēventum ī, n P. n. of evenio, an occurrence, chance, event : causae eventorum.— That which befalls, experience, fortune : te ex nostris eventis communibus admonendum: pendere ex alterius eventis.— An issue, consequenc…

eventura.definition: ēventūra ōrum, n P. n. of evenio, that which will happen : eventura precor, i. e. my prayers shall be fulfilled , Tb.

eversus.definition: ēversus. 1. P. of everro.— 2. P. of everto.

evidenter.definition: ēvidenter adv. evidens, evidently, manifestly, obviously : paenitere, L.

evito1.definition: ē-vītō āvī, ātus, āre, to shun, avoid: meta Evitata rotis, H.: fraxinum, O.: causas suspicionum: tela amictu, Ct.

evito2.definition: ēvītō āvī, —, āre ex + vita, to deprive of life, kill : Priamo vi vitam evitari, Enn. ap. C.

evocatus.definition: ēvocātus adj. P. of evoco, called out.— Plur. m . as subst, reënlisted veterans , Cs., S.

evolgo.definition: ē-volgō (-vulgō) āvī, ātus, āre, to make commonly known, divulge: civile ius, L.: sic evulgari iussit, laurum additum (esse), etc., Ta.: evolgatus pudor, i. e. public exposure, Ta.

evolsio.definition: ēvolsiō (ēvul-) ōnis, f ex + 2 VEL-, a pulling out : dentis.

exactus.definition: exāctus adj. with comp. P. of exigo, precise, accurate, exact : numerus, L.: fides, O.: morum exactior, O.—Plur n . as subst: sociis exacta referre, V.

exadversus.definition: ex-adversus (-vorsus) adv. and praep, over against, opposite.—As adv.: pistrilla, et exadvorsum fabrica, T.: exadvorsum ei loco Tonstrina erat, T.—As praep. with acc: exadversus eum locum: exadversum Athenas, N.

examen1.definition: exāmen inis, n ex + 1 AG-, a multitude flying out, swarm : apium: vesparum, L.: cum prima sui ducent examina reges, V.— A multitude, crowd, shoal, swarm : examinibus suis agros operire, L.: iuvenum, H.: servorum.

examen2.definition: exāmen inis, n ex + 2 AG-, the tongue of a balance : aequato examine lances Sustinet, V.—Fig., a weighing, consideration : legum, O.

exanimis.definition: exanimis e, adj. ex + anima, lifeless, dead : (columba) Decidit exanimis, V.: ut exanimem labentem ex equo Scipionem vidit, L.: artūs, O.— Fig., breathless, terrified, dismayed : legiones vice unius, with suspense for…

exardesco.definition: ex-ārdēscō ārsī, ārsus, ere, inch, to blaze out, kindle, take fire: materies facilis ad exardescendum.— Fig., to be kindled, be inflamed, break out, be exasperated, be provoked, rage: iracundiā ac stomacho: dolore, Cs…

excellens.definition: excellēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, towering, prominent, distinguished, superior, surpassing, excellent : animus ac virtus: vir virtute: inter tot unus: studium, Cs.: cycnus, of surpassing beauty …

excellentia.definition: excellentia ae, f excellens, superiority, excellence : animi.—Plur: (in amicitiā).

excelse.definition: (excelsē) adv. excelsus, in an elevated tone, loftily .— Only comp: excelsius dicere.

excelsus.definition: excelsus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, elevated, lofty, high : locus, T.: mons, Cs.: vertex montis, V.: signum: in excelsiore loco: cornu excelsius, Cs.: mons excelsissimus, Cs.—As subst n., a height : simul…

excessus.definition: excessus ūs, m 1 CAD-, a departure, demise : e vitā : Romuli.— A digression , Ta.

excido1.definition: excidō cidī, —, ere ex + cado, to fall out, drop down, fall away : sol excidisse mihi e mundo videtur: dentīs Excidere videre, H.: mihi Excidit cera, from my hand , O.: Palinurus Exciderat puppi, V.: in flumen (sc. e …

excido2.definition: excīdō īdī, īsus, ere ex + caedo, to cut out, cut off, hew out, cut down : arbores, Cs.: excisa arbor: columnas rupibus, V.— To raze, demolish, lay waste, destroy : aedīs: Troiam, V.: Sugambros, Ta.—Fig., to drive out…

excieo.definition: ex-cieō and ex-ciō īvī, ītus and itus, ī re, rarely ēre (imperf. excībat, L.), to call out, summon forth, rouse: consulem ab urbe, L.: animas sepulcris, V.: artifices e Graeciā, Cu.: Antiochum in Graeciam, L.: Volscos…

excitatus.definition: excitātus adj. with comp. P. of excito, lively, vehement, excited : sonus: clamor excitatior, L.: fortuna, rising .

excitus.definition: excitus and excītus P. of excieo and excio.

excors.definition: excors cordis, adj. ex + cor, without intelligence, without understanding, senseless, silly, stupid : anus: hoc qui non videt, excors est: admodum: turpis et excors, H.

excursus2.definition: excursus ūs, m 1 CEL-, a running out, running forth, excursion : excursūsque brevīs temptant (apes), V.— A sally, charge, inroad, invasion : militum, Cs.: subiti, Ta.

excusate.definition: (excūsātē) adv. excuso, without blame .— Only comp: excusatius excipere, Ta.

excussus.definition: excussus adj. P. of excutio, stretched out, stiff : lacertus, O.

exedrium.definition: exedrium (exhe-) ī, n , e)ce/drion, a sittingroom, parlor: exedria nova in porticulā.

exercitatus.definition: exercitātus adj. with comp. and sup. exercito; freq. of exerceo, well exercised, practised, versed, trained, experienced, disciplined : ad hanc rem, T.: in re militari: superioribus proeliis, Cs.: exercitatiores ad be…

exercitus1.definition: exercitus adj. P. of exerceo, disciplined , experienced, versed : miles: ad omne flagitium, Ta.: consuetudine velare odium, Ta.: militiā, Ta.: eloquentia, of a practised speaker , Ta. — Vexed, harassed : omnibus iniqu…

exercitus2.definition: exercitus ūs (dat. ū, Cs., L.; gen plur. tūm, L.) exerceo, a disciplined body of men, army : terrestris, L.: tiro, L.: pedester, N.: exercitum dimittere, T.: comparare: parare, S.: scribere, L.: contrahere, Cs.: ducer…

exheres.definition: ex-hērēs ēdis, adj., disinherited: paternorum bonorum filius.

exigue.definition: exiguē adv. exiguus, shortly, slightly, scantily, sparingly, exactingly, barely, meagrely : nimis exigue ad calculos revocare amicitiam: Praebent sumptum, T.: frumentum exigue dierum XXX habere, Cs.: epistula scripta.

exiliter.definition: exīliter adv., thinly, meagrely: verba exanimata: annales scripti: ad calculos revocare amicitiam, illiberally.

eximie.definition: eximiē adv. eximius, exceedingly, very much, uncommonly, excellently : Plotium dilexit: cenare, Iu.: polliceri omnia, L.

exin.definition: exin or (old and late) exim for exinde, adv. —In place, thence, after that, next in order, next : (mare) ... exin aër: exim ventum Elephantinen, Ta.— After that, thereafter, then : Exin compellare pater me voce videtu…

existimantes.definition: (exīstimantēs) ium, m P. plur. of existimo, critics, critical judges .

exitus2.definition: exitus ūs, m ex + 1 I-, a going out, going forth, egress, departure : omni exitu interclusi, Cs.: hominum exitū s adservare, Cs.: ne exitus inclusis ab urbe esset, L.— A way of egress, outlet, passage : angustus porta…

exlex.definition: ex-lēx ēgis, adj., beyond the law, bound by no law, lawless: exlegem esse Sullam putare: spectator, H.

exolesco.definition: ex-olēscō olēvī, ētus, ere, inch, to grow out of use, become obsolete, pass away, cease: cum patris favor exolevisset, L.: exoletis annalium exemplis, L.: exolescunt Graeci amictūs, Ta.: ne disciplina per desidiam exo…

exoptatus.definition: exoptātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exopto, greatly wished, earnestly desired, longed for : nuntius: parens, V.: nihil exoptatius adventu meo: exoptatissima gratulatio.

exorsa.definition: exōrsa ōrum, n 1 exorsus, a beginning, commencement : longa, preamble , V.: sua cuique exorsa laborem ferent, V.

exorsus2.definition: exōrsus ūs, m 1 OL-, a beginning, commencement : orationis.

exortus2.definition: exortus ūs, m 1 OL-, a coming forth, rising : solis exortūs, L.: lucis, Cu.

expedite.definition: expedītē adv. with comp. and sup. expeditus, without impediment, without difficulty, readily, promptly, quickly : explicans quod proposuerat: expeditius navigans: te expeditissime conferas.

expeditus.definition: expedītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of expedio, unfettered, unimpeded, unencumbered, without a burden : in Galliam proficisci: Sagana, tucked up , H.: legiones, without baggage , Cs.: expedito exercitu pervenit, Ta.…

expensum.definition: expēnsum ī P. n. of expensus, money paid, a payment : codex accepti et expensi, receipts and disbursements : tabulae accepti et expensi.

experiens.definition: experiēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of experior, experienced, enterprising, active, industrious : homo: vir, L.: experientissimus arator: genus experiens laborum, used to , O.

expertus.definition: expertus adj. P. of experior, tried, proved, known by experience : vir expertae virtutis, L.: libertatis dulcedine nondum expertā, L.: miles, Ta.: per omnia, L.— Experienced in : belli iuvenes, V.

expetendus.definition: expetendus adj. P. of expeto, worth striving for, desirable : gloria.

expetens.definition: expetēns entis, adj. P. of expeto, desirous, eager : in voluptatibus.

explanate.definition: (explānātē) adv. explanatus, plainly, clearly, distinctly .—Only comp: definire rem.

explanatus.definition: explānātus adj. P. of explano, plain, distinct : vocum impressio, i. e. ability to articulate .

expletus.definition: explētus adj. P. of expleo, full, complete, perfect : rerum comprehensio: undique forma honestatis.

explicatus1.definition: explicātus adj. with comp. P. of explico, spread out : planissimo in loco.— Well ordered : causa: provincia.— Plain, clear : solutio: quibus (litteris) nihil explicatius.— Assured, certain : ratio salutis suae.

explicatus2.definition: explicātus ūs, m explico, an unfolding, exposition : difficilīs explicatūs habere.

explicitus.definition: (explicitus) adj. P. of explico, unobstructed, practicable .—Only comp: (consilium), Cs.

explorate.definition: explōrātē adv. with comp. exploratus, for a certainty, securely, surely : haec scribo: exploratius promittere.

exploratus.definition: explōrātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exploro, ascertained, established, settled, certain, sure, safe : Iam id exploratumst, T.: consulatus: victoria, Cs.: litterae exploratae a timore, i. e. affording certainty :…

expolitus.definition: expolītus adj. with comp. P. of expolio, polished, smooth : expolitior dens, Ct.— Refined : vir vitā.

expositus.definition: expositus adj. P. of expono, open, accessible : Sunion, O.: Zephyris Lilybaeon, O. — Fig., common, vulgar : nihil expositum deducere, Iu.

expressus.definition: expressus adj. with comp. P. of exprimo, clearly exhibited, distinct, manifest, clear, plain, express : species deorum, quae nihil habeat expressi: litterae lituraeque. — Fig., distinct, real : signa virtutum: sceleri…

expromptus.definition: exprōmptus adj. P. of expromo, ready, at hand : malitia atque astutia, T.

exquisite.definition: exquīsītē adv. with comp. exquisitus, carefully, accurately, particularly, excellently : de eo crimine disputare: quae (rationes) exquisitius conliguntur.

exquisitus.definition: exquīsītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exquiro, carefully sought out, ripely considered, choice, excellent, exquisite : sententia: iudicium litterarum: munditia nimis: exquisitius dicendi genus: laudari exquisitiss…

exsecratus.definition: exsecrātus (execr-) adj. P. of exsecror, accursed, execrable, detestable : populo R.: columna.

exsiccatus.definition: exsiccātus adj. P. of exsicco, dried up, dry, jejune : orationis genus.

exsors.definition: ex-sors or exors sortis, adj., without lot, not assigned by lot: te voluit exsortem ducere honores (i. e. praeter ordinem), V. (al. honorem).— Having no share in, free from, deprived of: dulcis vitae, V.: amicitiae, L…

exspectatus.definition: exspectātus adj. with sup. P. of exspecto, anxiously expected, longed for, desired, welcome : carus omnibus exspectatusque venies: seges, V.: exspectati ad amplissimam dignitatem fratres, i. e. thought worthy of the h…

exspersus.definition: exspersus P. ex-sparsus, sprinkled, splashed : sanieque exspersa natarent Limina, V.

exspes.definition: ex-spēs adj. (only nom sing.), without hope, hopeless: inops, exspes, O.: enatat exspes, H.

exstructum.definition: exstrūctum ī, n exstructus, a lofty seat : exstructoque resedit, V.

exsuctus.definition: exsūctus P. ex-sugo, drawn out, extracted, dried : medulla, H.: Ossa exsucta medullis, Iu.

exsultans.definition: exsultāns (exult-) ntis, adj. P. of exsulto, boastful, vainglorious : animus, Ta.: supra modum, Ta.

extentus.definition: extentus adj. with sup. P. of extendo, extended, extensive, wide : latius Lucrino Stagna lacu, H.: extentissima vallis, L.

extenuatus.definition: extenuātus adj. with sup. P. of extenuo, trifling, faint, weak : vestigia, Ct.: oratio, Her.: (copiolae) extenuatissimae, Brut. ad C.

extergeo.definition: (ex-tergeō) —, sus, ēre, to strip clean, plunder: fanum extersum relinquere.

exterior.definition: exterior us, adj. comp. exter, outward, outer, exterior : vallus, Cs.: contra exteriorem hostem, Cs.: comes exterior, i. e. on the left side , H.

exterius.definition: exterius adv. exterior, on the outer side, without : sitae (urbes), O.

extimus.definition: extimus or extumus adj. sup. ex, outermost, farthest, most remote : orbis. — Plur n . as subst: umor Extuma possedit, O.

extortus.definition: extortus adj. P. of extorqueo, deformed , puella, Iu.

extra.definition: extrā adv. and praep. exter. I. Adv. (for comp. see exterius), on the outside, without : extra et intus hostem habere, Cs.: et in corpore et extra: illa, quae sunt extra, outward goods .—In the phrase, extra quam: ext…

extremo.definition: extrēmō adv. extremus, at last, finally Hamilcarem imperatorem fecerunt, N.

extremum.definition: extrēmum adv. extremus, at last, finally , C.: liquefacta Tabuit, O.— For the last time : te adfari, V.: Adloquor amicos, O.

extumefactus.definition: extumefactus adj. ex-tumeo + facio, swollen : (pars animi) potu (B. & K.).

exundans.definition: exundāns ntis, adj. P. of exundo, overflowing, abundant : ingenii fons, Iu.

exuvium.definition: exuvium ī, n 4 AV-, spoils, booty : exuvio plenus ab hoste redis, Pr.
